exposure: Age at presentation of intracranial haemorrhage (ICH) (<2 years, 1 month to 2 years, >2 years)
outcome: Risk of ICH after instrumental delivery compared to spontaneous vaginal delivery
cohort: 66 children (≤16 years old) with inherited bleeding disorders treated at UK haemophilia centres from 2003 to 2015
finding: Intracranial haemorrhage occurs most frequently in children with severe inherited bleeding disorders during the first 2 years of life and in children not receiving prophylaxis.
mod_finding: In children with haemophilia, the risk of ICH after instrumental delivery was 10.6 times greater than after spontaneous vaginal delivery.
